keys.statement: A classic sequencing heuristic, reported by the authors, leaves the most difficult split to last because it needs a high reflux ratio.

decisions.mechanism: A difficult split needs high reflux, cheaper with fewer components present.
decisions.expected_change: Lower energy for the difficult split.
limits: Reported by Li et al. as a classic heuristic, which they then qualify (see the disputed row).

keys.statement: Choose column pressure so the condenser can use cooling water rather than refrigeration, and set it together with heat integration.

decisions.obstacle: A low condenser temperature needs refrigeration.
decisions.mechanism: Higher pressure raises the condensing temperature.
decisions.operation: Raise pressure to the cooling-water level.

keys.statement: Shortcut column models (Fenske-Underwood-Gilliland) combined with heat-exchanger network synthesis screened distillation sequences reliably; only the best few needed rigorous simulation.

decisions.obstacle: Too many sequences to simulate rigorously.
decisions.mechanism: Shortcuts rank sequences as rigorous models do for zeotropic mixtures.
decisions.operation: Screen with shortcuts, verify the best rigorously.

keys.statement: Without heat integration, thermally coupled complex columns beat sequences of simple columns by a wide margin; once heat integration is included the difference narrows a lot.

decisions.obstacle: Choosing between complex and simple columns.
decisions.mechanism: Heat integration recovers much of what coupling saves.
decisions.operation: Compare complex and simple columns with heat integration included.
